points.description: Diffusion is net movement of particles from high to low concentration down gradient
points.source_quote:
Diffusion is the net movement of particles from an area of high concentration
to an area of low concentration, down a concentration gradient.
accept: net movement down a concentration gradient

points.description: Diffusion is passive needing no energy from cell
points.source_quote:
It is a passive
process: it needs no energy from the cell.

points.description: Osmosis is movement of water molecules across partially permeable membrane
points.source_quote: Osmosis is the movement of water molecules across a partially permeable membrane
accept: movement of water across selectively permeable membrane

points.description: Osmosis moves water from high to low water concentration down gradient
points.source_quote:
from an area of high water concentration to an area of low water
concentration (down a water potential gradient).

points.description: Substrate binds to enzyme active site (a)
points.source_quote: the substrate binds to the active site

points.description: Active site changes shape slightly moulding around substrate (a)
points.source_quote: the active site changes shape slightly, moulding itself closely around the substrate.
accept: active site flexes to fit substrate closely
reject: active site does not change shape

points.description: Strains substrate bonds or holds two substrates in right position so reaction easier (a)
points.source_quote:
This strains the substrate's bonds, or holds two substrates
together in exactly the right position, so the reaction happens far more
easily.
accept: stresses substrate bonds to weaken them
brings two substrates together in correct orientation

points.source_quote: The products are then released and the enzyme is unchanged.

points.description: Above optimum extra energy breaks weak bonds holding tertiary structure (b)
points.source_quote:
Above the optimum, the extra energy breaks the weak bonds that hold the
enzyme's tertiary structure together.
accept: heat breaks weak bonds in enzyme

points.description: Active site loses shape and enzyme denatured (b)
points.source_quote:
The active site loses its shape and the
enzyme is said to be denatured.
accept: active site shape destroyed by heat

points.description: Substrate no longer fits into denatured active site (b)
points.source_quote:
The substrate no longer fits, so the rate of
an enzyme-controlled reaction falls sharply at high temperatures.
accept: substrate cannot fit / attach to denatured active site
reject: substrate fits better at high temperature

points.description: Rate of enzyme-controlled reaction falls sharply at high temperatures (b)
points.source_quote:
so the rate of
an enzyme-controlled reaction falls sharply at high temperatures.

points.description: Plant cells have cellulose cell wall for support; animal cells do not
points.source_quote: A cell wall made of cellulose, which supports and strengthens the cell.
accept: plant has cellulose wall, animal has none
only plants have wall for support/strength

points.description: Plant cells have chloroplasts with chlorophyll for photosynthesis; animal cells do not
points.source_quote: Chloroplasts, which contain chlorophyll and trap light energy for photosynthesis.
accept: plant has chloroplasts, animal does not
only plants trap light for photosynthesis

points.description: Plant cells have large permanent sap vacuole keeping cell turgid; animal cells have only small temporary vacuoles if any
points.source_quote:
- A large permanent vacuole filled with cell sap, which keeps the cell turgid.
  Animal cells have only small, temporary vacuoles, if any.
accept: plants have large sap-filled vacuole, animals have small temporary ones

points.description: Losing nucleus leaves more room for haemoglobin
points.source_quote:
Losing the nucleus leaves more room
for haemoglobin,
accept: room for haemoglobin after losing nucleus

points.description: Haemoglobin is red pigment that binds oxygen
points.source_quote: for haemoglobin, the red pigment that binds oxygen,

points.description: So each cell can carry more oxygen
points.source_quote:
so each cell can carry
more oxygen.

points.description: Links loss of nucleus to small flexible size for squeezing through capillaries
points.reason: Notes link squeezing through capillaries to biconcave shape, not to loss of nucleus; need lecturer confirmation if this link is creditable
